content.thinking:
I'm planning out the qilin quadruped rig in one careful pass without testing incrementally—sketching dimensions (roughly 1.5m shoulder height, 2m length), then structuring the skeleton with a hip root joint, spine chain running to chest/neck/head, and a separate tail chain extending backward from the hips.

Still defining joint chains...

For the body, I'll sweep along the spine chain path with varying radii to create a barrel shape, then add separate sweeps for the neck and tail chains, letting the round caps overlap to hide seams. For materials, I'm planning a jade-teal scale pattern for the body with a cream-gold underbelly, flowing cream/aqua mane, and gold antlers for a classic qilin look.

Now I'm defining the scale paint shader with layered teal tones and a countershading gradient toward the cream underbelly, then moving to leg placement with inverse kinematics -- setting shoulder and foot positions for the front legs and working out segment lengths to ensure proper reach.

I'm working out the joint bend directions for a quadruped's limbs: elbow bending backward with carpus forward on the front legs, and stifle forward with hock backward on the hind legs, naming each chain joint for the IK setup.

Then I'm parenting each leg chain to the correct spine or hip bone, positioning the side offset by a sign multiplier, and setting up the sweep radii that taper from thigh to foot for a smooth leg silhouette, with a separate piece planned for the hoof shape.

Limb target set with foot resting near the ground, checking hip-to-foot reach adds up across hind leg segments. Now planning fur tufts at the fetlocks using flame and cloud wisp textures on cards, positioned at the knee frames along the leg sweep.

For the mane, I'm considering using overlapping flattened spheres along the neck's dorsal line to create cloud-like lumps in creamy white, attaching them via bone weights so they follow the neck sweep naturally.

Designing the plume texture as a simple curling SVG shape with white fill and aqua inner strokes. For the tail, I'm planning a four-joint chain with plume card fans at the end plus extruded flame blades for flair. For the head, I'm sketching a dragon-like skull with a scaled sphere, frustum snout, and separate jaw, positioned relative to a head joint defined off the neck's end direction.

Writing head placement code...

Adding whiskers trailing back from the snout, a chin beard tuft, small white teeth spikes on the upper jaw, and eye decals placed via surface coordinates mirrored across the skull with amber "gold-fire" iris coloring.

Now I'm building branching antlers sprouting from the skull's crown, using a hit point on the skull's surface and a catmull path defined in head-local coordinates, mirroring the left/right placement based on side.

Each antler sweeps up and back as a main beam with two or three smaller tines branching off at points along the curve, colored gold with glowing cyan tips. I'm also considering adding torus ring bands along the beam for texture, oriented using the curve's frame at each point.

Next I'm working out the ears as extruded leaf-shaped fins on the sides of the head, pointing backward with a defined thickness and outline shape.

I'm also planning the cheek frills similarly, plus a glowing cyan forehead gem, skipping the nose horn, and setting up a dorsal ridge of gold/cyan cone fins placed along the spine using the body's sweep path.

I'm also weighing whether to add flame-wisp card details on the shoulders and legs, deciding to keep that minimal, and instead focusing on scale rows and a gold collar ring built around the neck joint.

Placing a small gold pendant bell offset down and slightly forward from the neck. Now I'm working out the spine curve points from hips through mid to chest, and setting up ellipse radii at each level to shape the body barrel.

Extending the body silhouette toward the tail and neck with rounded caps that overlap smoothly, then plotting the neck curve from chest up to the head joint with tapering radius, and positioning the head with a forward-downward direction so the tip lands roughly where the muzzle should be.

I'm sketching out the tail points trailing back from the hips, continuing the chain structure for the joints.

For the tail tuft I'll add a ring of frames near the tail tip to generate plume cards, placing another ring further along for coverage, and note that the hips joint doubles as the root with spine1 sharing its position. Now I'm moving on to the body skin using a sweep.

Building the leg sweep code...

Checking leg lengths and hip-to-target distances for front and hind limbs to make sure they stay within reach, adjusting bend directions so knees point forward and hocks point back. For leg coloring I'm setting up a gradient paint fading to gold near the lower leg, wrapped in cel shading to match the toon style.

For the eyes, I'm placing them as decals on the skull sphere using spherical coordinates (azimuth/elevation) around the head's center, positioning them symmetrically at roughly ±55° azimuth and 8° elevation, and checking how the decal's default direction gets set when using the "at" targeting.

Now I'm working out the whisker geometry, tracing catmull-rom spline paths from points near the snout outward and backward using local head-relative offsets, sweeping tubes along these curves with a tapering radius.

I'm also setting up jaw coloring: a cel-shaded cream head tone, a darker gold nose pad, and a lighter teal for the lower jaw to contrast against the upper jaw's coat shade.

Adding fangs and interior details...

Still defining jaw geometry... I'm also sketching a goatee tuft sweeping down from the chin tip and brow ridge sweeps above each eye using mirrored left/right offsets.

Now adding a small glowing octahedron gem for the forehead, positioning it relative to the skull's ellipsoid shape so it sits correctly on the front-top surface.

Then working out antler placement, starting from a surface point near the skull crown and building a path of points relative to the head to shape the antler beam geometry.

Still working out the frame and bone attachment logic...

Still defining tine geometry...

Adjusting ring radius based on path position, then moving to the cloud mane geometry—placing dorsal clumps of spheres along the neck sweep curve at varying angles and scaling them to taper naturally.

I'm setting up mane color variations with cycling cel-shaded hues, then generating wisp card textures along the neck curve with outward-facing frames and flow directions flattened to follow the surface slope. Now I'm starting on the plume texture SVG for the tail.

Writing SVG wisp shape...

Finishing the flame texture for legs, then planning gold spiral cloud scroll decals for the body flank.

Deciding to mirror the decal when s<0, then placing two decals per side at the shoulder and haunch with different sizes, positioned near the body surface. Now I'm planning dorsal spine fins as a row of cones running along the body.

Adding fin cones along spine...

Deciding to skip belly plates and chest tufts since countershading and mane already cover those areas, and sketching hoof caps, fetlock flame cards, and leg tufts as spikes at the hock and knee.

Still placing flame cards...

Now I'm assigning chain roles like spine, neck, tail, and leg so each part knows its purpose, including head and jaw joints. For the hooves, I'm sizing a tapered cylinder in gold tones and positioning it so the leg's rounded tip sits snugly inside.

Still placing leg roots... working out foot x/z offsets for front and hind legs so they stay within the body's silhouette, naming spine and shoulder bones per side, and starting a sweep function to shape the body profile along its length.

Now I'm adding mane cards along the neck sweep at various clock angles for a flanking effect, and planning helper functions inside the build while being careful about strict TypeScript unused-variable errors.

I'm pruning my import list to only what's actually needed—builder utilities, offset/rng for card placement, catmull curves, limb and paint helpers, scales/countershade, svg, and the toon shading pieces like animeEye, cel, INK, and glow. Then I'm placing small nostril spheres on the head bone using inked coloring, positioned near the nose tip.

Now I'm working out the upper jaw shape, tapering it with radius functions as it extends forward, and considering whether to add cheek frills extruded outward from the head for a dragon-like fin effect.

Adjusting the ear outline to sweep back and up along the skull, checking it stays non-self-intersecting, then thinking about adding a cream inner-ear color and moving on to the eye socket decal placement.

I realize that since joint directions are model-forward rather than bone-forward, head tilt doesn't actually affect my placement logic, which simplifies things. I'm now positioning the jaw joint and its aim direction relative to the head, sweeping the lower jaw from there.

Still working out skull-jaw overlap at the back, then shifting attention to the eye details and finishing the head paint shader setup using a smaller-scale cel-shaded pattern.

Now I'm adding whiskers in paired sets with slight offsets, plus a chin tuft made of a few spiky sweeps anchored to the jaw bone. I'm also sanity-checking the overall part count and triangle budget, and confirming ground contact so hooves sit at y=0 while the tail stays above it.

I still need to cap the flat color palette under 64 and decide on glow elements—maybe octahedron gems at the gem/tine/eye spots—plus check whether the anime eye helper accepts a false blush option. I'm also considering gold anklet torus rings and thin cyan rune bands along the legs for extra detail.

Working out the anklet placement, I'm matching the torus radius against the tapering leg radius so the ring sits snugly near the hoof, then adding small gold bracers at the shoulders and hips. A gold pendant bell at the neck collar could round out the chest decoration.

Adding collar and bell geometry...

Still working out limb chains, parenting, and sweep radii for legs...

Setting up imports and style metadata, then defining paint logic so leg socks get a different color below a height threshold...
